topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture, connects it to earlier practicals, and sets out what the lecture will cover.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the cellular origin of oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor-causing viruses led to the discovery that transforming viral genes originate from cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes laboratory methods for testing whether genes or mutations can transform cells.

topics.label: Functional classifications of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets out the categories used to describe mutations by their effects on tumor growth and cellular maintenance.

topics.label: Mutation effects on RB and p53 growth control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations disrupt growth control, through the RB-regulated cell-cycle checkpoint and mutation-specific effects on p53.

topics.label: Genetic instability: repair, replication, and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation produce genetic instability and affect tumor cells.

topics.label: Mutation timing in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the timing and order of mutations, including chromosomal instability, relate to colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes inherited cancer risk through mutations affecting genomic integrity or growth control, with examples of hereditary syndromes.

topics.label: BRCA2 restoration and malignancy despite repaired instability
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic uses BRCA2 restoration during treatment to show that genetic instability is not required for a cancer to remain malignant.

topics.label: Lecture close and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by inviting questions, recommending reading, and previewing the next lecture.
